headline_summary: Astera Labs is the connectivity-silicon company built by three TI alumni in November 2017, IPO'd on NASDAQ in March 2024, that in FY2025 doubled revenue to $852.5M at 75.7% GAAP gross margin and $219M GAAP net income — a structural-margin level associated with software more than silicon. The board has been assembled with rare deliberation (chair Manuel Alba ex-Galileo/Marvell, Craig Barratt incoming Intel chairman, Michael Hurlston current Lumentum CEO, Stefan Dyckerhoff of Sutter Hill, Bethany Mayer ex-Ixia/Box chair, Jack Lazar ex-GoPro CFO) and the balance sheet carries $1.19B of liquid against essentially no debt.
structural_thesis_in_one_paragraph: Astera Labs is the rare connectivity-silicon company that has reached $850M+ of annual revenue at 75.7% GAAP gross margin within seven years of founding and two years of being public. The investment question is whether the FY25 result — 115% revenue growth, structural-margin discipline, GAAP profitability, fortress balance sheet — sustains through the Nvidia Rubin / AMD MI400 architecture transition where design-in position must be re-won at a new generation of accelerator GPU. The board composition (chair Manuel Alba's connectivity-M&A pattern recognition, Craig Barratt's incoming Intel chairmanship, Michael Hurlston's current Lumentum CEO seat, Stefan Dyckerhoff's Sutter Hill venture chair, Jack Lazar's audit-grade CFO experience, Bethany Mayer's HPE/Box/LAM Research breadth) is configured for cycle-compression governance through that transition rather than for additional IPO-execution or financial engineering.
